title: Hund's rule: nitrogen and oxygen
caption: In nitrogen the three 2p electrons occupy separate orbitals with parallel spins. Oxygen's fourth 2p electron must pair, and the repulsion within that pair makes it easier to remove: oxygen's first ionisation energy (1314 kJ mol⁻¹) is below nitrogen's (1402).
alt: 2s and 2p boxes for nitrogen, three single parallel electrons in 2p, and oxygen, one paired and two single 2p electrons.
description: Nitrogen, 2s² 2p³: three 2p boxes each with one up arrow.
Oxygen, 2s² 2p⁴: the first 2p box paired, the other two singly occupied.
